area: memory and initiative: core/memory (optmem, life, capture, judge, loops, loop-tool, tools), server initiative/, room/memory.ts, room/memory-naps.ts, room/signals.ts, user/memory-capture.ts
purpose: Keep a bounded, correctable memory of the human (chat summaries, life facts, open loops) and let Yuki raise open loops and promises at the human's usual time without nagging.
summary: The memory core (OptMem tree, life log, loops store, recall, private-chat gating) is sound and well tested: freeze it. The initiative stack is heavier than a few-user product needs: a learned appetite, a weekly rhythm histogram, a hand-weighted score and an LLM worth judge all decide one nudge, and facts and loops each have two capture paths. One real bug silently drops a second agent promise in a nap span, which hits users with no judge key.

subareas.name: Chat memory tree and recall
subareas.why: Bounded view, sticky tiling for prompt-cache reuse, idempotent naps. Tested by optmem, log-memory, memory-rules, recall-agent. Nits: test-only exports in prod, 60-step bisection in cover().

subareas.name: Life log, card, pins, supersede, redact
subareas.why: Real user surface (view, pin, redact). Supersede and redact-by-ref restore prior lines correctly. Tested by life-capture. Pre-launch migrations are cruft.

subareas.name: Loops store and Jev burst classifier
subareas.why: Merge, close and redaction are solid. Agent promises use a ref dedupe that collapses distinct nap loops (problem 1). Jev closes are not room-scoped. Loops come from three extractors.

subareas.name: Fact capture: judge path and model path
subareas.why: Two capture paths do the same job, picked by a three-way mode. The model path is measured in docs as finding nothing. The judge path calls once per message and resends every criterion per question.

subareas.name: Attention: appetite, rhythm, score, gating
subareas.why: Gating is well tested and the caps are clear. Speculative layers: per-kind Beta appetite, 168-slot rhythm, hand-tuned score weights, a judge that restates the same signals. Per-item ignore counts never decay.

subareas.name: Initiative engine: marks, wakes, pass, brief
subareas.why: Idempotent result handling and stable wake ids. No setTimeout, no DO waits in receive(). Marks, briefed and wakes tables are never pruned, and all of initiative_marks is read on every agent brief.

subareas.name: Routine signal window
subareas.why: Batching and redelivery are sound. But two signal kinds are never consumed, and a DROP TABLE runs on every construction.

strengths: Private chats are gated at every write: capturable(), title null for private chats, PRIVATE_REFUSAL on the note tool.
Judge failures return null and fall back; a refused key is marked and stops being used.
Idempotency is designed in: nap_applied keyed by span and prompt hash, deliveries.seen for wakes, attention_seen for bursts, pending-status check in ran().
SQL lists use json_each; no per-item binds in this area. No setTimeout in these files.

Broad tests: server attention, initiative-runs, initiative-safety, loops, memory-capture, life-capture, log-memory, optmem, memory-rules, recall-agent; CLI suites initiative, memory-jev, memory-edge, memory-eval, memory-isolation, proactive, team-loops, token-cost.

problems.title: A second agent promise in one nap span is silently merged into the first
problems.evidence: core/memory/src/loops.ts:132-135 returns merged for any non-tool, non-human open with the same ref, owner and room. initiative.ts:80 gives every nap loop ref room:<id>:turns:lo-hi, so all promises in one 16-turn page share a ref. Reproduced with bun against the real Loops class (/tmp/audit/repro/nap-ref.test.ts): 'send the deck to Rafael' is new (id 1); 'book the room for Thursday' comes back merged into id 1; the live list holds only the first. loops.test.ts:119 only tests parsing. With no judge key, nap is the only path that records agent promises.
problems.fix: Scope the ref dedupe to source jev. For nap, dedupe on norm only. Add a loops test with two promises under one nap ref.

problems.title: Fact capture makes one judge request per message, not per burst
problems.evidence: user/memory-capture.ts:183-189: captureNow loops over queued rows (up to 24 per alarm) and calls captureWithJudge for each. Loops batch one classify per chat.
problems.fix: Batch the capture queue into one classify per alarm, tagging each candidate with its message index. This cuts round trips and the Free subrequest budget (50 per invocation).

problems.title: Capture judge request repeats every criterion per question
problems.evidence: core/memory/src/capture.ts:101-103 adds two questions per known fact; NEIGHBORS=8 (line 66) allows 6 x (3 + 16) = 114 questions per message. pi-ai sends each question object whole (node_modules/@earendil-works/pi-ai/dist/api/system-one-shared.js:108-115), so SAME and REPLACES criteria repeat per fact. The docs' 'state written once' fix does not cover criteria. A TypeSafe question cap is UNVERIFIED.
problems.fix: Put criteria in state once and reference them by path, or cut NEIGHBORS. Measure with bun yuki verify token-cost before and after.

problems.title: Per-item ignore count never decays, so a nudged item can be muted for years
problems.evidence: attention/appetite.ts:65: rest = lastSurfaced + cycle * 2**ignored * (0.5/p). initiative_marks is never pruned (engine.ts:156). Arithmetic: with a daily cycle and p near 0.5, ten ignores give about 1024 days of rest. The appetite fades with a 14-day half-life; this count does not.
problems.fix: Cap the exponent (for example 2**min(ignored, 3)) or fade it with the appetite half-life. Add a test that a loop ignored ten times is nudged again within a year.

problems.title: Forgetting an edit or delete makes one DO call per turn, and a failed batch never advances
problems.evidence: room/memory-naps.ts:62 awaits user.forgetRoomTurn once per position; forwarded(changes.upto) runs only after the loop (line 66). A batch over the subrequest budget throws, retries in 30 s, and sees the same changes, so deleted text stays in life and loops.
problems.fix: Batch positions into one UserDO call. Whether DO stub calls count against the budget is UNVERIFIED; the loop is unbounded either way.

problems.title: Jev can close an agent's promise in another chat
problems.evidence: initiative.ts:52 calls deps.close(op.id, status, at); initiative-loops.ts:60 closes with no roomId, so loops.ts close() skips the room filter. The loop tool passes its room. A human's 'that's done' in chat A can close an agent's promise in chat B.
problems.fix: Decide the intended scope. If the room must match, pass the loop's room; otherwise document it.

problems.title: Two signal kinds are emitted and never consumed
problems.evidence: reminder_fired and watch_change are emitted at user/reminders.ts:537 and :587 and sent to UserDO.signals (user-do.ts:113). engine.signals and routineRun ignore them; reports.ts:60 returns early without a burst, agent_final, task or file. Schema at room/signals.ts:16-17.
problems.fix: Delete both kinds and their emit sites, or give them a trigger.

problems.title: Initiative tables grow without limit, and marks are read in full on every brief
problems.evidence: initiative_marks, initiative_briefed and initiative_wakes have no DELETE. engine.ts:156 reads all of initiative_marks in items(), which noticed() reaches on every agent run. Task marks are keyed by updatedAt, so each change adds a row.
problems.fix: Read marks only for current candidates (WHERE id IN json_each(?)) and prune rows older than the appetite half-life.

problems.title: Signal window clears overflow counts when a batch is sent
problems.evidence: room/signals.ts:143 DELETE FROM signal_more clears all of it, including overflow added while the batch was in flight.
problems.fix: Subtract the sent count instead of clearing.

problems.title: Nap pass may exceed the Free subrequest budget (UNVERIFIED)
problems.evidence: room/memory-naps.ts NAPS_PER_PASS=24. Each nap is a UserDO compress call plus a model fetch, plus rollups, against 50 per invocation. Failures are caught and retried, so it self-heals.
problems.fix: Confirm with wrangler tail whether DO stub calls count, then cap NAPS_PER_PASS to fit.

overengineering.title: Second capture path: model-based 'always' mode
overengineering.evidence: core/memory/src/capture.ts:149-234 (capturePrompt, parseCapture, applyOps); user/memory-capture.ts:221-244 captureByModel and the fallthrough in captureNow. architecture.md:783 records that the base path found no new fact in 30 turns and cost 4 to 7 extra calls.
overengineering.why: Two paths do the same job, and the code's own measurement says the model path cost more without finding facts. Drop 'always' (the owner's call) or keep one path. captureNow mixes both today.

overengineering.title: Two judge calls per human burst (loops and facts) on the same text
overengineering.evidence: initiative-loops.ts hear() queues loop_heard (15 s, one call per chat); memory-capture.ts captureHuman() queues capture_queue (3 s, one call per message).
overengineering.why: Different questions, but one classify request per burst with two question sets halves judge round trips. Do it when either queue is next touched.

overengineering.title: Three loop extractors: Jev, nap loop lines, loop tool
overengineering.evidence: core/memory/src/loops.ts napLoopsPrompt and parseNapLoops (about 90 lines) run in every nap, even when Jev has read the same burst. initiative.ts napApply.
overengineering.why: The nap path is the right no-judge fallback (KEEP). With a judge key, skip loop lines in the nap prompt to save tokens. Fix problem 1 first.

overengineering.title: Per-kind Beta appetite learning
overengineering.evidence: attention/appetite.ts:1-92: posterior, fade, kindOpen, kindMean, allowance, settle, learn, WEIGHTS. A new kind starts at mean 0.5, sd 0.29, so kindOpen holds until several ignores (arithmetic, not run).
overengineering.why: With few users the per-kind counts barely move in a 14-day half-life, so the gate is probably inert. A per-user ignore counter with a cap does the job. Check real counts before removing kinds.

overengineering.title: Rhythm: 168-slot weekly histogram with pooling and smoothing
overengineering.evidence: attention/rhythm.ts:1-121: rates() pools hours across weekdays, 3-tap smoothing, 28-day half-life, MIN_EVIDENCE 10, cycle from moment spacing.
overengineering.why: The pacing idea is earned (KEEP moments and the active window). A 24-slot hour-of-day histogram would give the same moments for most users at about half the code.

overengineering.title: Two deciders for one nudge: hand-weighted score and LLM worth
overengineering.evidence: attention/attend.ts:17 WORTH=0.5; :54 jev ?? s; :64 worth = (jev ?? s) * min(1, kindMean/0.5). score() at :24-41 has four constants. Worth criteria in initiative/judge.ts:32-35 restate the due, promise and stale signals the score already encodes.
overengineering.why: The judge overrides the score in worth, yet the score still gates the brief reasons. The docs say the engine is the one decider; the code has two. Pick one.

overengineering.title: Dead signal kinds and their emit sites
Test-only helpers and one-shot migrations in production code
overengineering.evidence: optmem.ts:88-100 isNode and ancestors, used only by optmem.test.ts and log-memory.test.ts; room/signals.ts:95 DROP TABLE routine_windows on every construction; optmem.ts Tree drops a 'tainted' column; life.ts NORM_VERSION rewrite.
overengineering.why: Move helpers into tests. Delete one-shot migrations once no pre-launch data is kept. No behavior change.

overengineering.title: KEEP: OptMem tree, life log, loops store, rerank
overengineering.evidence: core/memory/src/optmem.ts (cover, tile, Tree), life.ts, loops.ts store, memory-capture.ts rerank.
overengineering.why: Each answers a measured need: bounded context, stable prompt prefix, correction and redaction, a no-judge fallback. Do not refactor for style.

CLI (model keys): initiative, initiative-loops, memory-jev, memory-edge, memory-eval, memory-isolation, memory-session, memory-hard, memory-tools, proactive, team-loops, token-cost.
